traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for 010.3-DEV-MIGRATE-TO-SUPPORTS are implemented and verified: - **Optional Warning & Configurable Enforcement (REQ-OPTIONAL-WARNING, REQ-CONFIG-SEVERITY):** The `traceability/prefer-implements-annotation` rule is implemented as a suggestion rule, disabled by default (not present in recommended/strict presets), and its behavior is controlled solely via ESLint severities (off/warn/error). Tests explicitly confirm default-off behavior and configurable severities. - **Auto-fix Support & Single Story Conversion (REQ-AUTO-FIX, REQ-SINGLE-STORY-FIX):** The rule includes a conservative auto-fix that, for exactly one `@story` and one-or-more simple `@req` lines, rewrites them into a single `@supports ` line. Tests verify both the single-REQ and multi-REQ conversions with expected output. - **Multi-story Detection & Non-fixable Cases (REQ-MULTI-STORY-DETECT, REQ-VALID-OUTPUT):** The implementation detects mixed legacy/@supports comments and multi-story comments and emits `cannotAutoFix` or `multiStoryDetected` messages without providing a fix. Tests cover both mixed-usage and multi-story patterns, matching the story’s described behavior. - **Preserve Order / JSDoc Structure (REQ-PRESERVE-FORMAT):** The fixer reconstructs the comment body by replacing only the `@story` line with an equivalent `@supports` line, preserving the original line prefix (indentation and `*`) and leaving all other lines and their order unchanged. This maintains the relative placement of annotations within the JSDoc block. - **Both Formats Valid & Backward Compatibility (REQ-BACKWARD-COMP-VALIDATION):** The rule’s logic only reports when a comment has both `@story` and `@req`; it ignores comments with only `@story`, only `@req`, or only `@supports`. Dedicated tests confirm those patterns are treated as valid and unreported, and additional tests confirm the rule is not enabled in built-in presets, so existing validation rules continue to govern `@story`/`@req` unchanged when this migration rule is off. - **Quality of Output (REQ-VALID-OUTPUT):** Auto-fix only applies when `@story` and `@req` lines are in simple, tokenized forms; otherwise the fixer is suppressed and only a recommendation is reported. This conservative approach ensures generated `@supports` annotations are structurally valid and consistent with existing validation expectations. - **Documentation:** Both the internal rule docs and the user-facing migration guide document the rule’s purpose, configuration, behavior, auto-fix examples, and limitations, matching the story’s documentation acceptance criteria.
Given the dedicated implementation, comprehensive tests tied directly to this story, successful test run, and aligned documentation, the story is fully implemented and passes all specified acceptance criteria.
